study: Hitchcock et al. 2011, Collaborative Strategic Reading (CSR), NCEE/REL Southwest RCT
eval_evidence: Formally an IES/NCEE REL Southwest contractor evaluation (NCEE 2011-4001). Caveat: CSR co-developer Dr. Joseph Dimino is a report co-author and delivered the training/trained the coaches (Instructional Research Group); the report itself notes contractors' work 'may not be entirely independent.' Coded independent on the REL/NCEE structure but flagging the co-developer's central involvement.
developer_evidence: 'CSR codeveloper, Dr. Joseph Dimino, provided an initial two-day training session to teachers' — the developer (also a report co-author) personally delivered the core teacher training.
cascade_evidence: The developer (Dimino) trained the teachers directly in the initial two-day session; he also trained the coaches who delivered four follow-up coaching sessions, but the teachers' primary PD was developer-to-teacher direct (no intermediary trainer for the core training).
counterfactual_evidence: Control was a business-as-usual condition: control classrooms used 'the school's normal instructional procedures' for social studies. No active alternative program.
coaching_evidence: Beyond the two-day initial training, trained coaches 'provided four follow-up coaching sessions to the teachers throughout the year' (fall + spring) — a few periodic coaching/observation visits, i.e. light/occasional support, not monthly+/biweekly+ in-class cycles.
student_dose_evidence: Teachers used CSR strategies when delivering their regular social-studies curriculum; only the teacher's regular instruction changes, no added tutoring/pull-out/extra-minutes or student-facing software dose.
maturity_evidence: Implementation period was one school year; teachers were newly trained in CSR and outcomes (GRADE) measured at the end of that single first implementation year.
